summary.oneLiner: India Cements' turnaround under UltraTech is now visible in the P&L, not just on a slide: EBITDA/ton has climbed sequentially and unbroken from ~Rs 386 (Q2FY26) → Rs 400 → Rs 509 → **Rs 603 this quarter**, on **+21% like-for-like revenue** (Rs 993 cr ex-factory vs Rs 821 cr LY) and **+19% volume**, with brand migration to UltraTech **100% complete**. Management reaffirmed a clear path to **Rs 1,000/ton EBITDA for India Cements by Q4FY28** as ~Rs 2,000 cr of cost-improvement capex (WHR, preheater/cooler) and a green-power step-up (3% → ~86% by FY28) flow through. Parent UltraTech printed a **record first quarter** (domestic volume +13.1%, EBITDA Rs 5,146 cr +12%, PAT Rs 2,604 cr +17.2%) and reaffirmed the cables & wires launch in Q3FY27.
summary.business: The Company manufactures and sells cement and clinker, an activity that accounted for 98.15% of turnover in FY 2025-26, with cement/clinker products contributing 99.05% of total turnover. It operates 16 plants and 9 offices in India across 14 states, with no international operations and nil exports. It sells to trade customers (end consumers building homes), non-trade/institutional customers such as infrastructure companies executing roads, dams, airports and real estate projects, and OEMs such as hollow block, paver tile and concrete pipe manufacturers.

currentContext.expansion: The Directors' Report and the MD&A 'Going Forward' section both state that the Company proposes to incur / is incurring capital expenditure to the extent of `2,014 crore over a period of two years. This comprises expansion of the existing capacity by 2.80 Million Tonnes, from 14.75 Million Tonnes to 17.55 Million Tonnes, at an estimated cost of `440 crore, and modernization of the Company's cement plants at an estimated cost of `1,574 crore. The proposed capital expenditure would be met through a mix of debt and internal accruals. No individual plant, line or site is named for the expansion and no commissioning date is given beyond the stated two-year period. Separately, the Directors' Report records that cement capacity utilization during FY 26 was 70% compared to 62% in FY 25, and the Company completed the migration of its product brands to the brand portfolio of its holding company during the year.
currentContext.mdna: India projected to remain one of the fastest-growing major economies with GDP growth moderating to around 6.5%, driven mainly by domestic demand and sustained public infrastructure spending|India remains the second largest cement market in the world, with structural demand from urbanisation, infrastructure creation, housing and an expanding industrial base|Industry installed cement production capacity at the close of FY 26 stood at 718 million tonnes per annum; independent agencies estimate 100 million tonnes of new grinding capacity will be commissioned over the two years ending FY 28|Domestic cement demand during FY 26 grew by 6.4%; for FY 27 industry estimates converge in the range of 6.0 to 7.5% year-on-year growth, with leading rating agencies placing growth at 6 to 7% and 7 to 8% respectively|Cement industry expected to witness healthy mid-to-high single-digit demand growth supported by infrastructure, housing and urban development|Rising fuel and freight costs may pressure margins in the near term; large players with scale, diversified fuel mix and operational efficiencies are seen as well positioned to sustain growth|Long-term sector fundamentals remain strong, with consolidation and capacity additions reinforcing resilience|Three external factors flagged for close monitoring: crude oil and petroleum coke prices amid geopolitical developments, the South-West Monsoon against below-normal projections and its impact on rural demand, and United States tariff policy changes affecting the rupee and the cost of imported inputs|Increasing government spending on infrastructure and improvement in demand in housing markets seen as positioning the Company to strengthen its presence in its core markets

risks.note: With the regulatory framework constantly evolving with more compliance and legal requirements particularly on emissions and sustainability, the industry is exposed to stringent controls and penalties. The Company mitigates through investment in pollution control equipment for CO2, SOx, NOx and other greenhouse gas emissions, with all plant pollution control equipment linked in real time to the State Pollution Control Boards.

risks.risk: Raw material availability, supply vulnerability and cost volatility
risks.note: Limited availability of key raw materials, geopolitical tension, supply chain vulnerabilities and volatility in input costs may disrupt production continuity and adversely affect long-term operating costs. Cement manufacturing is energy and raw-material intensive and exposed to securing long-term availability, particularly with changing laws under the Mines and Minerals Development and Regulation Act (MMDR); availability of quality raw material and fuel at affordable prices is an area of concern. Mitigants cited are an optimum mix of indigenous and imported coal, stepped-up alternate fuels, adequate limestone reserves with mining licenses and long-term fly-ash contracts.

risks.risk: Fuel and freight cost inflation compressing margins
risks.note: Management states that rising fuel and freight costs may pressure margins in the near term, and separately flags movements in crude oil and petroleum coke prices amid geopolitical developments as a factor requiring close monitoring.

risks.risk: Demand sensitivity to monsoon and government infrastructure spending
risks.note: The performance of the South-West Monsoon, in the light of below-normal projections, and its impact on rural demand is one of three external factors management flagged for close monitoring; demand outlook is otherwise tied to infrastructure, housing and urban development spending.

risks.risk: Macro / trade policy and currency exposure
risks.note: Changes in United States tariff policies, along with their effect on the rupee and the cost of imported inputs, is explicitly flagged as an external factor requiring close monitoring.

Higher dependence on information technology has increased cyber security risk; data safety, integration and process technology are prone to attack which can impact business operations and all assets. Mitigation is via vulnerability studies, third-party impact assessment audits, back-up systems for critical servers, firewalls, threat-protection software and employee training.

risks.risk: Human resources - talent retention and attrition
risks.note: Retaining talented manpower is described as a challenging task for the industry; the Company is taking steps to lower attrition, improve the working environment and systematically review training needs.

Health and safety incidents across high-risk operations may result in legal exposure, operational disruptions and adverse reputational impact; the BRSR discloses recordable work-related injuries and high-consequence injuries among workers during the year, managed through an ISO 45001-aligned OHS system, the Fatal-6 framework and Board-level oversight.

guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
**India Cements-specific (logged as INDIACEM commitments):**
- **EBITDA Rs 1,000/ton "very much in sight" by Q4FY28** — with full benefit of the capex programme flowing through the P&L.
- **Green power 3% → ~86%** of India Cements' power requirement by end of FY28.
- **Cost-improvement capex ~Rs 2,000 cr** being deployed (waste-heat recovery, preheater upgradation, cooler upgradation).
- **ICL integration/merger to complete by Q4FY28** (or a quarter earlier) — pending capex completion + non-core land (asset) disposal + bringing operating parameters in line with UltraTech standalone.
- Q2FY27 to look "optically softer" (seasonal monsoon + West Asia cost weigh).

**Parent UltraTech (context — belongs under ULTRACEMCO, not logged here):**
- Double-digit domestic grey volume growth targeted for FY27; industry Q1 volume ~7–8%.
- Q2FY27 cost +Rs 130–140/ton sequentially (fuel + kiln maintenance + operating deleverage).
- Capacity: 205.5 MT total now → grey 212.7 MT by FY27-end → ~235 MT (India) by Mar'28; consolidated > 242 MT; capex ~Rs 17,000 cr over 2–2.5 yrs (all internal accruals).
- Green power 1,897 MW (47% of power at quarter exit) → 2.5–3 GW "very shortly."
- **Cables & Wires: commissioning + product launch reaffirmed for Q3FY27 (Oct–Dec'26)**; Rs 1,800 cr programme, Rs 888 cr spent/committed; aluminium from Hindalco (4-hr lead).
- UltraTech Rs 1,400/ton EBITDA target: Jan–Mar'28 quarter "without any war."
order book & pipeline: - Not an order-book business. Demand pipeline framed as very rich: cement-intensive projects called out — Maharashtra Rs 20,000 cr shipbuilding cluster (Mazagaon Dock), Odisha Rs 50,000 cr+ deep seaport/shipbuilding (Ganjam/Paradip), Tamil Nadu ~Rs 18,000 cr data-centre/shipbuilding MoU, Ahmedabad-Dholera semi-HSR (~Rs 20,000 cr), Rs 30,000 cr NIIF infusion, Vadhavan port (packages awarded), Ken-Betwa river-linking. Housing/urban real estate = ~55–60% of consumption, strong start to CY26 (Mumbai registrations +6%).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **India Cements:** the turnaround centrepiece — EBITDA/ton Rs 603, brand migration 100% done, conversion ratio 1.5x, ~Rs 2,000 cr efficiency capex underway, green power headed 3%→86% by FY28. Merger into UltraTech standalone targeted Q4FY28.
- **Regional (UltraTech, this quarter):** East slowest (elections/labour); South & North a shade below 15%; West & Central above 15%. East seen inflecting structurally over next 2–4 years (land reforms, elections done).
- **Cables & Wires (new business):** facility complete, trial runs commenced, channel partners onboarding, regulatory approvals in place; launch Q3FY27; will "mature and milk" before any further capex.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Cables & Wires the new growth engine (Q3FY27 launch); "sky is the limit" but no guidance — "profitable, grounded, grow with the market."
- Premiumization + blended-cement mix compounding blended realisations regardless of headline price. RMC only ~3.5% of UltraTech sales (retail 65–66%, institutional ~35%) → India remains a *branded* cement market (analogous to branded steel/paints) as long as it's an individual-homebuilder/retail market.
- Beyond 240 MT: team already "on the drawing board"; inorganic opportunities to be examined.
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona:
- **Brand premium in a retail market:** UltraTech converted India Cements/Kesoram B/C-category customers to A-category willing to pay a premium — brand volume +21.3%; did not vacate the value space, migrated it up. Evidence: 76 operating facilities, ~2,000 warehouses, 150,000 channel partners, 477 RMC plants, 5,000+ UBS stores, ~50%+ dedicated transporters — a distribution/brand density "nobody else can come close to."
- **Secured raw material:** "every ton of committed expansion is fully backed by secured limestone" — no raw-material constraint on the growth path.
- **Cost buffers:** green power (47% of power at exit, cheaper), lead distance down to 360 km (from 367), clinker conversion 1.5x — structural cost advantages that let UltraTech "absorb the shock better than any peer and harvest relief faster."
margins & cost dynamics:
- Held per-ton EBITDA essentially flat (> Rs 1,200) while growing absolute EBITDA +12% — "cost discipline + operating leverage as designed," on a base enlarged by still-ramping acquired assets.
- Cost headwinds: fuel +5% (Rs 874→915/ton), packing bags (Rs 9→~12/bag, the bigger Q1 hit), industrial diesel +~50% (Rs ~100→150s/litre) spiking limestone-raising cost (highest in 2 yrs). Pet coke now costlier than coal in energy terms → shift to domestic coal. Q2 cost +Rs 130–140/ton sequentially, then H2 relief hoped as war/freight normalise (ocean-freight insurance 1% → 4–5%).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Group capex ~Rs 17,000 cr over 2–2.5 yrs → consolidated capacity > 242 MT; grey 212.7 MT by FY27-end, ~235 MT India by Mar'28. FY26 deployed ~Rs 9,500 cr. This quarter 8.7 MT of new UltraTech capacity commissioned (Shahjahanpur, Visakhapatnam, Patratu) → 205.5 MT total. India Cements ~Rs 2,000 cr efficiency capex. Cables & Wires Rs 1,800 cr (Rs 888 cr spent), launch Q3FY27 — all reaffirmed "on schedule, on budget."
capital allocation: - Operating cash flows fully ploughed back into cement growth + dividends; "no requirement for further investment in cables & wires" for now. Dividend policy = percentage of profits ("expecting good dividends"). Net debt/EBITDA 0.87x, target < 1x. Growth funded by internal accruals.
risks & watch-items:
- **West Asia / fuel:** Strait of Hormuz shock, crude > USD 100; full cost hits Q2FY27; timing uncertain. Ocean-freight insurance up to 4–5%.
- **Monsoon/dry spells:** Rajasthan very dry (water-crisis demand risk *next* year); Q2 seasonal slowdown + kiln maintenance.
- **India Cements execution:** Rs 1,000/ton EBITDA + merger both hinge on capex flowing through by Q4FY28 — slippage watch.
- **Pricing:** monsoon-quarter prices expected "broadly steady"; cost pass-through of last 2 quarters still incomplete.
management quality / tone: Very confident, delivery-focused, mildly immodest by design. Track record emphasised: crossed 200 MT a year early, completed India Cements/Kesoram brand migration a quarter early, and reaffirmed cables & wires for Q3FY27 — "we deliver what we commit." Candid on cost pressure and Q2 optics ("look through the noise"). India Cements framed explicitly as a promise-turned-trajectory (EBITDA/ton progression given quarter-by-quarter).
non-obvious takeaways:
- India Cements' revenue *decline* is a reporting artefact (ex-factory switch), masking +21% like-for-like — a trap for a headline reader.
- The India Cements green-power leap **3% → 86% by FY28** is the single biggest, least-appreciated cost lever behind the Rs 603 → Rs 1,000/ton EBITDA path.
- UltraTech has *stopped reporting India Cements standalone volumes* — entire ICL volume now folded into UltraTech's number, signalling the merger endgame (Q4FY28).
- The Rs 1,400/ton UltraTech EBITDA "magical number" is explicitly pinned to Jan–Mar'28 "without any war" — a management-set, verifiable milestone.
- Coal has overtaken pet coke on energy economics → the fuel-mix shift to domestic coal is a margin tailwind if it holds.

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and sells cement and clinker, an activity that accounted for 98.15% of turnover in FY 2025-26, with cement/clinker products contributing 99.05% of total turnover. It operates 16 plants and 9 offices in India across 14 states, with no international operations and nil exports. It sells to trade customers (end consumers building homes), non-trade/institutional customers such as infrastructure companies executing roads, dams, airports and real estate projects, and OEMs such as hollow block, paver tile and concrete pipe manufacturers.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India projected to remain one of the fastest-growing major economies with GDP growth moderating to around 6.5%, driven mainly by domestic demand and sustained public infrastructure spending
- India remains the second largest cement market in the world, with structural demand from urbanisation, infrastructure creation, housing and an expanding industrial base
- Industry installed cement production capacity at the close of FY 26 stood at 718 million tonnes per annum; independent agencies estimate 100 million tonnes of new grinding capacity will be commissioned over the two years ending FY 28
- Domestic cement demand during FY 26 grew by 6.4%; for FY 27 industry estimates converge in the range of 6.0 to 7.5% year-on-year growth, with leading rating agencies placing growth at 6 to 7% and 7 to 8% respectively
- Cement industry expected to witness healthy mid-to-high single-digit demand growth supported by infrastructure, housing and urban development
- Rising fuel and freight costs may pressure margins in the near term; large players with scale, diversified fuel mix and operational efficiencies are seen as well positioned to sustain growth
- Long-term sector fundamentals remain strong, with consolidation and capacity additions reinforcing resilience
- Three external factors flagged for close monitoring: crude oil and petroleum coke prices amid geopolitical developments, the South-West Monsoon against below-normal projections and its impact on rural demand, and United States tariff policy changes affecting the rupee and the cost of imported inputs
- Increasing government spending on infrastructure and improvement in demand in housing markets seen as positioning the Company to strengthen its presence in its core markets

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Directors' Report and the MD&A 'Going Forward' section both state that the Company proposes to incur / is incurring capital expenditure to the extent of `2,014 crore over a period of two years. This comprises expansion of the existing capacity by 2.80 Million Tonnes, from 14.75 Million Tonnes to 17.55 Million Tonnes, at an estimated cost of `440 crore, and modernization of the Company's cement plants at an estimated cost of `1,574 crore. The proposed capital expenditure would be met through a mix of debt and internal accruals. No individual plant, line or site is named for the expansion and no commissioning date is given beyond the stated two-year period. Separately, the Directors' Report records that cement capacity utilization during FY 26 was 70% compared to 62% in FY 25, and the Company completed the migration of its product brands to the brand portfolio of its holding company during the year.
